rules_applied: key sort: UTF-16 code-unit lexicographic order (ECMA-262 default string compare, NOT locale or case-insensitive collation): 'C'=U+0043 < 'a'=U+0061 < 'b'=U+0062 — the uppercase key sorts first solely because its code point is numerically smaller
whitespace stripped: object punctuation is ',' and ':' only (RFC 8785 §3.2.2.3)
integer values 1,2,3 pass through unchanged in ECMAScript integer notation
canonicalization is recursive: key sorting applied at every object level, including objects nested inside arrays
array element order preserved (arrays are ordered values, never sorted)
true/null emitted as lowercase literal tokens
n1: 1e21 -> 1e+21 (ECMA-262 Number::toString switches to exponential for |x| >= 1e21; lowercase 'e', explicit '+')
n2: 1e-7 -> 1e-7 (exponential notation for |x| < 1e-6)
n3: 0.000001 -> 0.000001 (exactly at the 1e-6 boundary, fixed decimal notation is retained)
n4: 1e20 -> 100000000000000000000 (integer-valued, magnitude < 1e21, plain integer notation)
n5: -0 -> 0 (IEEE-754 negative zero renders as '0'; ToString(-0)='0', RFC 8785 §3.2.2.3 forbids '-0')

n6: 333333333.33333329 -> 333333333.3333333 (literal parsed to nearest IEEE-754 binary64 double, re-emitted as shortest round-tripping decimal; 16 significant digits, since 15 digits .333333 is ~4.9 ULP away)
keys n1..n6 already in code-unit order (common prefix 'n', then U+0031..U+0036)
key sort by UTF-16 code units: '$'=U+0024 < 'a'=U+0061 < 'ü'=U+00FC < '€'=U+20AC, so order is $, aa, ü, €

comparison is on code units only — not UTF-8 byte order, not locale collation, not case folding: 'ü' precedes '€' because 0x00FC < 0x20AC (the UTF-8 encodings C3 BC vs E2 82 AC happen to order the same way, but code-unit order is the governing rule)
non-ASCII keys/values emitted as raw UTF-8 bytes, no \uXXXX escapes
LF U+000A -> \n (bytes 5C 6E), short-form escape per RFC 8785 §3.2.2.2
HT U+0009 -> \t (bytes 5C 74)
QUOTATION MARK U+0022 -> \" (bytes 5C 22)
é U+00E9 emitted literally as UTF-8 bytes C3 A9 — no \uXXXX for non-ASCII, no surrogate conversion
U+0020 space is NOT escaped: JCS escapes only U+0022, U+005C, and C0 controls U+0000–U+001F; any other control char would appear as \u00xx with lowercase hex digits
keys s1..s5 already in code-unit order, so the compact and canonical strings coincide byte-for-byte here

weakest_point: Case 5, key s5: the two trailing characters arrived as literal U+0020 spaces, which JCS emits unescaped; if the reference input actually contained raw C0 control characters there (stripped in transport), the expected bytes would instead contain \u00xx lowercase-hex escapes. The rule in doubt is exactly which code points constitute s5's value (literal-space passthrough vs. control-character \u00xx escape handling).
